data.title: Telling Time by Fives

challenges.instruction: Look at the clock face. The long minute hand points to a number representing minutes by fives. Match it to the correct digital time.
challenges.hint: Remember that each number on the clock face counts as 5 minutes for the long hand. 3 times 5 is 15.

challenges.instruction: Find the matching digital time for this clock. Notice where both the short hour hand and the long minute hand are pointing.
challenges.hint: When the long minute hand points straight down at the 6, it has traveled 30 minutes around the clock.

challenges.instruction: Read the clock carefully by counting the minutes in groups of 5 around the dial. Select the matching digital time.
challenges.hint: Count by fives starting from the 12. The minute hand is past the 9, so it is 45 minutes past the hour.

challenges.instruction: Examine this clock face showing minutes counting by fives. Choose the correct digital display.
challenges.hint: The hour hand is almost at the 2, and the minute hand is almost all the way around at the 11. That means 55 minutes.

challenges.instruction: Put your skills together to find the correct digital time for this analog clock showing a 5-minute interval.
challenges.hint: The short hand is past the 5, and the long hand is pointing at the 4. Count by fives four times to find the minutes.

data.description: Students practice reading analog clocks and matching them to digital times using 5-minute intervals.
